result.summary: Warn users when the post-encryption database rewrite fails during wallet encryption. A failed rewrite leaves plaintext key material in unused database pages, so the wallet logs an explicit warning advising funds be moved while preserving the successful encryption state.
result.problem: When encrypting a wallet, a failure during the final database rewrite step is silently ignored. Users assume their at-rest wallet data contains only encrypted keys, while uncompacted storage pages may still retain recoverable plaintext key material.
evidence: PR description: 'Wallet encryption ignores a failed database rewrite after encrypted key records have been committed. Old plaintext key material can remain in unused pages without a warning.'
result.scope_notes: Small patch (+30/-2) consisting of a test characterizing the rewrite failure and a warning log in the wallet encryption path.
result.card: This PR adds a warning when the final database rewrite fails during wallet encryption. When this rewrite step fails, plaintext key bytes can remain in uncompacted database pages even though the wallet marks encryption as successful. Logging this warning alerts users to transfer funds to a newly created wallet before assuming keys are safe at rest. No dependencies.

risk.why: The patch only adds a warning log and a regression test without altering the wallet encryption flow or transaction handling.
